title: Evaluate typed decision routing
summary: Define the decision, representative cases and uncertain-result behavior before choosing a model-backed route.

sections.label: Use this workflow
sections.text: Use when a process needs a bounded choice, score or yes/no-style assessment. A deterministic rule or human decision may be sufficient. Laya is an optional model candidate, not a replacement selected by Atlas.

sections.label: Inputs
items: Question, allowed outcomes, decision owner and cost of each error.
Representative labelled cases, incomplete inputs and language/domain scope.
Pinned model/checkpoint, actual deployment interface and routing limits.

sections.label: Repository contributions
sections.text: Laya documents typed choice, score and yes/no-style assessments and a router that selects checkpoints. A typed result or confidence value does not establish correctness, calibration or permission to execute an action.

sections.label: Procedure
items: Write the decision and expected result for concrete normal, ambiguous and failed cases.
Compare a simple rule, current approach and selected model only where each can perform the same task.
Pin the checkpoint and input/outcome format. Inspect truncation and option handling on representative inputs.
Measure each important error class and uncertainty behavior, not only aggregate accuracy.
Define what happens for missing evidence or an uncertain result. Keep action authorization separate from the predicted choice.
Retain a conditional recommendation and the evidence. Do not replace an existing backend until its own relevant cases have been compared.

sections.label: Outputs
sections.text: A decision contract, comparison cases, observed errors and a routing recommendation with explicit limits.

sections.label: Acceptance checks
items: Expected outcomes were reviewed independently of candidate predictions.
Relevant languages, domains, ambiguous states and denied actions were included.
A score or probability is interpreted according to its actual contract.
An untested model choice is labelled proposed.

sections.label: Illustrative example
sections.text: For billing triage, agree the permitted department labels and when a human must review an ambiguous complaint. Compare predictions with reviewed labels before proposing automatic routing. No Laya or Atlas backend comparison has run in this example.

basis: Inspected repository documentation and recommended Atlas procedure. Examples are illustrative.
confidence: Moderate for the scoped source contributions. Project fit and workflow outcomes remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Define the decision, representative cases and uncertain-result behavior before choosing a model-backed route.
catalog.limits: Reading guidance does not install a repository, select a tool, execute a workflow or establish a passing result. Use actual project versions, commands and evidence.

claims.text: Laya documents typed choice, score and yes/no-style assessments with checkpoint routing.
